record.paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
record.original_question: Let G=(V,E,ω) be a weighted graph with landmark set L⊂V and witness set W⊂V. For the Dowker complexes built from G, study stability in two directions. First, if G'=(V,E,ω') has the same vertices and edges as G but a different weight function ω', bound the bottleneck distance between the persistence diagrams of the Dowker complexes of G and G' in terms of the supremum distance between ω and ω'. Second, if L and L' are both ε-nets for G, find conditions under which Dow_α(W,L) and Dow_α(W,L') have the same homotopy type.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1.4. Let G = (V, E, ω) be a weighted graph and let L, W ⊂ V be sets of landmarks and witnesses for G. (i) Let G' = (V, E, ω') be the metric graph with the same set of vertices and edges of G, but another weight function ω'. Find a bound for the bottleneck distance of the persistence diagrams corresponding to the Dowker complexes of G and G' in terms of the supremum distance between ω and ω'. (ii) If two sets of landmarks L and L' for G are -nets. Find conditions on the landmarks, such that Dowα(W, L) and Dowα(W, L') have the same homotopy type.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E, ω) be a finite connected weighted graph, where ω : E → (0, ∞) assigns positive weights to edges. The weighted graph induces a shortest-path (pseudo)metric d_G on V. Fix two subsets L ⊂ V (landmarks) and W ⊂ V (witnesses). For a scale parameter α ≥ 0, the Dowker complex Dow_α(W, L) is the simplicial complex on the vertex set L whose simplices are the finite subsets σ ⊂ L such that there exists w ∈ W with d_G(w, ℓ) ≤ α for every ℓ ∈ σ. Letting α vary yields the Dowker filtration of (W, L) in G, whose persistent homology produces a persistence diagram Dgm(G; W, L).

A subset L ⊂ V is called an ε-net for G if for every v ∈ V there is some ℓ ∈ L with d_G(v, ℓ) ≤ ε, and any two distinct points of L are at distance more than ε. For two weight functions ω, ω' on the same edge set E, define the supremum distance ‖ω − ω'‖_∞ = max_{e ∈ E} |ω(e) − ω'(e)|.

(i) (Stability under reweighting.) Let G = (V, E, ω) and G' = (V, E, ω') be weighted graphs with the same vertex and edge sets, and fix L, W ⊂ V. Establish an explicit bound of the form
   d_B(Dgm(G; W, L), Dgm(G'; W, L)) ≤ C · ‖ω − ω'‖_∞,
where d_B denotes the bottleneck distance between persistence diagrams, and identify the optimal constant C (possibly depending on combinatorial features of G).

(ii) (Stability under change of landmarks.) Let L, L' ⊂ V both be ε-nets for G, and let W ⊂ V be a fixed witness set. Determine combinatorial or metric conditions on (L, L', W, G, α, ε) that guarantee Dow_α(W, L) and Dow_α(W, L') have the same homotopy type.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem on stability of Dowker complexes. Recent work (e.g., on functorial Dowker theorems, asymmetrically weighted Dowker persistence, and persistent path diagrams) addresses related stability statements for Dowker filtrations on networks, but none provides the explicit bottleneck bound in terms of the supremum weight-distance for landmark/witness Dowker complexes on weighted graphs, nor the homotopy-type criterion for differing ε-nets. The problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Asymmetrically Weighted Dowker Persistence and Applications in Dynamical Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Stability of Dowker persistence on weighted (directed) networks is studied, with bounds in terms of network distances.
status_evidence.claim: Related stability results exist but do not resolve the specific landmark/witness formulation on weighted graphs.

status_evidence.title: A functorial Dowker theorem and persistent homology of asymmetric networks
status_evidence.snippet: Stability of Dowker filtrations with respect to network distance.
status_evidence.claim: Provides general stability framework but does not give explicit supremum-weight bound or homotopy criterion for ε-net landmark changes.
